Country.evidence_source: “The total sample initially comprised 14,056 participants who completed the YBIS between September and December 2012, of whom 11,321 were US residents and 2,735 were non-US residents.”; “Non-US residents originated from 135 different countries (113 participants did not provide information about their country of residence). Of these participants, only three countries provided participants above a 5 % threshold, namely Canada (22.0 %), United Kingdom (14.2 %), and Australia (5.3 %). We, therefore, limited our analyses in the non-US sample to residents of these three countries.”; “Therefore, the final datasets comprised 8,925 US residents and 742 non-US residents.”

Sample.evidence_source: “Following ethical stipulations, we excluded from analyses participants who were under 18 years of age (n = 3,058). Furthermore, we only used participants who provided complete datasets with regard to the hypothesized model, leaving 8,925 US residents and 1,900 non-US residents.”; “We, therefore, limited our analyses in the non-US sample to residents of these three countries. Therefore, the final datasets comprised 8,925 US residents and 742 non-US residents.”

section_summary.extract_value: This Participants section describes an initial sample of 14,056 respondents to the YBIS (11,321 US, 2,735 non-US), exclusion of those under 18 and incomplete datasets, resulting in final datasets of 8,925 US residents and 742 non-US residents. Non-US participants originated from many countries but analyses were limited to Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia (the only non-US countries above 5%). The section does not label any study number (no 'Study 1' etc.) and reports BMI ranges but not mean BMI or demographic breakdowns by gender—detailed characteristics are reported in Table 1.
